subject: Covid-19
description: Order Re Protective Face Coverings in Court Facilities
issuer: Multnomah County Circuit Court — Presiding Judge
title: Multnomah County Circuit Court Presiding Judge Order — 2101-00000 (5); Covid-19
text:
IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE STATE OF OREGON
FOR MULTNOMAH COUNTY
In t he Matter of Implementing
Chief Justice Order No. 21-025
PRESIDING JUDGE ORDER NO. 2101-00000
ORDER RE PROTECTIVE FACE COVERINGS IN
COURT FACILITIES
On March 8, 2020, Oregon Governor Kate Brown issued Executive Order 20-03 decla ring a state
of emergency due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The state of emergency has been extended, but it is
scheduled to expire on June 28, 2021. On June 25, 2021, Governor Brown issued Executive Order 21-15,
which extended the state of emergency until December 31, 2021, but lifted the protective face covering
requirements, social distancing and other restrictions effective June 30, 2021.
On June 1, 2020, I issued Presiding Judge Order (PJO) 2001-00000, requiring all persons ent ering
court fac ilities in Multnomah County to wear protective face coverings. On October 28, 2020, Oregon
Chief Justice Martha Walte rs issued Chief Justice Order (CJO) 20-045, requiring protective face coverings
in all state court faci lities.
On June 28, 2021, Chief Justice Walters issued CJO 21-025, which lifted many restrict ions
previously imposed on court operations following the expiration of the state of emergency. CJO 21-025
lifts the protective face cove rings requirement previously imposed under CJO 20-045 and aut horizes
Presiding Judges in each judicial district to impose protective face covering requirements consistent with
county requirements or as needed to protect public health and safety.
On June 29, 2021, Multnomah County Chair Deborah Kafoury announced t hat protective face
coverings would continue to be required for staff working in county faci lities, and would be
recommended for members of the public entering county faci lit ies, until August 1, 2021,
notwit hstanding Governor Brown's action generally lifting the protective face covering requirement
statewide.
Accordingly, pursuant to the authority stated in CJO 21-025, consistent with Multnomah County
policy and to protect public health and safety, I hereby ORDER as fo llows:
1. Definitions. "Courthouse" means the common areas open to the public--including without
limitation hallways, elevators, the jury assembly room, public service counters, and other public
areas, and individual courtrooms-in the Mult nomah County Courthouse, the Juvenile Justice
Center, the Downtown Justice Center, and the East County Courthouse. "Protective face
1
covering" means a covering of the nose and mouth to protect against spreading the COVID-19
virus, as recommended by the Centers for Disease Control.
2. Except for witnesses while testifying, children under two (2) years of age, and as provided in
paragraphs 3 and 4 below, all persons entering the Courthouse are required to wear a
protective face covering while in the Courthouse.
3. A judge presiding over a trial or other proceeding in a courtroom may, in the judge's sole
discretion, allow any person participating in or attending the proceeding to remove the
protective face covering upon showing proof that the person has been fully vaccinated against
the COVID-19 virus. A judge may also al low jurors during voir dire to temporarily remove their
protective face covering to the extent the judge deems the removal appropriate for the jury
selection process. Judges and court staff who have been fully vaccinated are not required to
wear protective face coverings in the courtroom during a court proceeding.
4. Any person seeking to enter the Courthouse without using a protective face covering because of
disability, respiratory or other health-related issues, or otherwise for good cause can request an
exemption from the Presiding Judge. Exemption requests may be presented to the Presiding
Judge at the times set for ex parte matters or other times as needed. Persons requesting such
an exemption should contact Presiding Court before entering the Courthouse.
5. The Court will continue to provide protective face coverings and information about how to use
them as needed and as available resources allow.
6. This ORDER is effective on June 30, 2021, and will remain in effect until August 1, 2021, unless
extended by further order of this Court.
DATED: June 29, 2021
Stephen . Bushong
Presiding Judge, Multnomah County Circuit Court

IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE STATE OF OREGON
FOR MULTNOMAH COUNTY
I·e,the matter of Preventative PRESIDING JUDGE ORDER
2101-30000

Security Release in Cases Subject ORDER RE PREVENTATIVE
DETENTION HEARING
PROCEDURES AND SECURITY
RELEASE IN VIOLENT
FELONIES
ORS 135.240(2) to (4) and

ORs 135.240(6)
ORS 135.240(2) to (4) and ORS 135.240(6) provide for denial of pretrial release in
certain cases for individuals charged with violent felonies. This order describes the
procedures for determining preventative detention in charges subject to ORS 135.240(2}
to (4) and ORS 135.240(6). This order does not affect any procedure for any other charges
in the same or any other charging instrument related to the defendant if the charges are
not subject to this order.
For the crimes of Aggravated Murder, Murder in the First Degree, Murder in the
Second Degree, and Treason, the decision whether to set a security amount will be
deferred pending a hearing pursuant to the procedures set forth in ORS 135.240(2) to (4).
Until that time, the charge will be listed as "security decision deferred/no release."
The charges listed below are considered to be violent felonies for purposes of ORS
135.240(6) based on the charging instrument. For those charges, the decision whether to
set a security amount will be deferred pending further hearing pursuant to the
procedures set forth in ORS 135.240(4) (hereinafter Preventative Detention Hearing) or
other court order. Until that time, the charge will be listed as "security decision
deferred/no release."
• Any felony included in ORS 163A.005(5} (felony sex crimes)
• Manslaughter in the First Degree under ORS 163.118
• Manslaughter in the Second Degree under ORS 163.125
• Criminally Negligent Homicide under ORS 163.145
• Assault in the First Degree under ORS 163.185(1)(a), (b), or (d)
• Attempted Assault in the First Degree under ORS 163.185(a) or (b), or under ORS
163.185(d) if the person is accused of acting intentionally
• Assault in the Second Degree under ORS 163.175(1)(a) or (c)

subject: Covid-19; Jury
issuer: Multnomah County Circuit Court — Presiding Judge
title: Multnomah County Circuit Court Presiding Judge Order — 2101-00000 (10); Covid-19; Jury
text:
IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE STATE OF OREGON
FOR MULTNOMAH COUNTY
In the Matter of Implementing
Chief Justice Order No. 21-035
PRESIDING JUDGE ORDER NO. 2101-00000
ORDER RE REMOTE JURY SELECTION
On July 30, 2021, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued Guidance to the
effect that local decision-makers should assess certain factors to inform the need for prevention
strategies to minimize preventable morbidity and mortality related to COVID-19, including the level of
COVID-19 transm ission, health system capacity, vaccination coverage, capacity for early detection of
increases in COVID-19 cases, and populations at risk for severe outcomes from COVID-19. While
emphasizing t hat vaccines are the most effective tool to prevent transmission of COVID-19, the CDC also
has stated that multiple interventions should be used concurrently to reduce transmission and
recommends social distancing as one such mitigating measure.
Beginning on August 13, 2021, as a result of the rapid and extensive spread of the highly
contagious Delta variant of the COVID-19 virus, Governor Brown has announced a series of measures
designed to prevent the spread of the virus and to mitigate the risk to and impacts on public health and
statewide hospital capacity. Those measures have included statewide requirements to wear protective
face coverings both indoors and outdoors, with exceptions, and a vaccination requirement for state
executive branch employees. Governor Brown has cited new modeling from the Oregon Health
Authority (OHA) and the Oregon Health and Science University projecting that, without new health and
safety interventions in place, COVID-19 hospitalizations would far exceed Oregon's health system
capacity within the next several weeks.
On August 24, 2021, Governor Brown announced that the Delta variant had created a level of
crisis not yet seen during the pandemic in Oregon, with cases of COVID-19 and hospita lizations
statewide at a record high. The variant also has significantly impacted court operations across the state.
On August 26, 2021, I issued a Presiding Judge Order (PJO) extending the "Transition Period" through
October 31, 2021. Under that PJO, the protective face covering requirement is extended until at least
November 1, 2021, and most civil jury trials will be postponed until on or after November 1, 2021. On
September 7, 2021, Chief Justice Martha Walters issued Chief Justice Order (CJO) No. 21-035, requiring
social distancing for all public areas of a court proceeding, including courtrooms.
The social distancing requirement significantly limits th is court's ability to conduct jury trials
because of the limited space available for socially distanced jurors in the court's jury assembly room.
Consistent with CJO No. 21-035, I have concluded that the best way to implement socia l distancing,
protect the public, and continue to meet the court's obligations is to require juror selection to be
,.....
N
0
2,..3... °' -;;;
C: ·a
8....

conducted via remote means to the greatest extent possible. Conducting jury selection via remote
means allows the court to continue to hold jury trials while minimizing the number of people required to
appear in person in the courthouse. Minimizing the number of people summoned to appear in court for
jury duty and socially distancing those people who do appear in court in person would help minimize the
risk of spreading the virus while still allowing the court to conduct jury trials as needed. The court now
has the technological capability to conduct jury selection via remote means, thereby eliminating the
need for hundreds of people to appear in person for the j ury selection process each week.
Accordingly, it is hereby ORDERED as follows:
l. For trials in criminal and civil cases beginning on or after October 4, 2021, jurors will be
summoned to appear via remote means (currently, Web Ex) for jury selection. The court will
allow jurors who are unwilling to appear remotely or who lack the technical capability to
part icipate remotely to appear in person in the courthouse. The prospective jurors who
appear in person will participate in jury selection via remote means from a location within
the courthouse under circumstances that comply with the CJO and CDC Guidance. The
court will adopt appropriate procedures for conducting the jury selection process remotely,
including procedures for conducting trials in the event technological or other barriers
interfere with remote j ury selection.
2. Jurors selected to serve as jurors and alternate jurors for a particular trial shall be required
to appear in person for the remainder of the tria l, unless the parties have stipulated to and
the court has ordered a fu lly remote jury trial. Protective face coverings shall be required
for the trial as specified in my August 26 PJO, and social distancing shall be required for the
trial as specified in CJO 21-035.
3. Remote jury selection appl ies to j urors and prospective jurors only. Al l other participants in
the jury selection process-lawyers, parties, and the judge-shall appear in person in the
courtroom for the jury se lection process, unless the parties have stipulated to and the court
has ordered a fully remote jury trial. The trial itself will be conducted in t he courtroom in
accordance with Oregon law.
This order takes effect immediately and shall remain in effect until extended or terminated by
further order of this court.
DATED: September lQ_, 2021
Presiding Judge, Multnomah County Circuit Court

To achieve consistency with the eligibility rules of publicly funded programs for cash grants, nutrition

IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT Multnomah County Trial Court Administration staff making initial
determinations regarding eligibility for fee waivers and fee deferrals for court costs shall supplement the
definition of "household" adopted by Chief Justice Order 10-045 dated August 26, 2010, ('"Household'
means a person or group of people occupying a common dwelling and sharing necessary living
expenses") with the following:
"Sharing necessary living expenses" includes but is not limited to situations in which persons occupying a
common dwelling customarily purchase and prepare meals together. A single dwelling may contain more
than one household, each functioning as a single financial unit whose members share living expenses.
When the party requesting a fee deferral or waiver is adverse to a party named in the action for which fees

Having previously ordered the Multnomah County Circuit Court closed due to inclement weather
conditions on January 11, 2017 and January 12, 2017, having previously found good cause to extend the
time for preliminary hearings, and being aware that all grand jury proceedings were likewise canceled due
to weather, the court enters this blanket ORDER resetting dates.
All cases that were previously scheduled to have a preliminary hearing or arraignment on an indictment in
Justice Center Courtroom #3 on January 11, 2017, January 12, 2017, or January 13, 2017 are hereby set
for a preliminary hearing date of January 18, 2017, which will result in an arraignment on the resulting
indictment, if any, at 9:30 on January 19, 2017 in Justice Center Courtroom #3.
The court finds good cause based on the court closure and grand jury cancellations to extend the period
for the preliminary hearing in each case by the amount necessary to set the dates indicated above.
